name: ram-headed snake

attributes.attribute: carries the horn of a ram
changed by Christianity into a mark of evil
keeps the rite of the horned god

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The ram-headed snake was a sign of Continental Celtic religion. It united the ram horn and the body of a snake. In Christian teaching this image turned to evil, not power. The horned devil in later art descends from this Celtic form. Some festivals still hold the rites of the horned god. The feast at Abbots Bromley follows that ancient line.

okr.objective: Ram-headed snake is a Continental Celtic horned sign whose meaning shifted.
key_results: The ram-headed snake unites a ram horn and a serpent body.
Christian teaching turned this image toward evil, not might.
The horned devil of later art comes from this Celtic form.
The Abbots Bromley festival carries forward horned-god rites.
